headline: Organize push events by the frequency level they reach
statement: Implement FreqStack with push(val) and pop(). pop removes a value having the highest current frequency; on a frequency tie, remove the value whose most recent remaining occurrence was pushed last. The trainer constructs FreqStack once, then executes operations such as ["push",5] and ["pop"]. push returns None, displayed as null in the output list; pop returns the removed value.
constraints: At most 20,000 push and pop calls
pop is called only on a nonempty stack
intuition: Organize push events by the frequency level they reach. The top of the highest-frequency group is also the most recent event among tied values.
approach: Count the frequency of each pushed value.
Append it to the stack for its new frequency and update the maximum frequency.
Pop the latest entry from the maximum-frequency stack and decrease that value’s count.
If that group becomes empty, decrease the maximum frequency.
correctness: A push at level f records the moment a value gained its f-th active occurrence. These level-f entries remain in chronological order. The greatest nonempty level equals the greatest current frequency; its final entry is the most recent among tied values. Removing it exposes the correct previous-frequency history in lower groups, preserving the invariant.
bruteForce: Keep an ordinary list and recompute frequencies and search backwards on every pop: O(n) per operation.

complexity.explanation: Time O(1) amortized per operation; auxiliary space O(number of active pushes). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: A simple heap needs stale-entry management; frequency alone does not encode recency.
Do not remove the lower-frequency history when popping a top level.
Decrease max frequency only after its group empties.
